facts.text: The Australian king parrot lives only in eastern Australia, from Cooktown in Queensland down to Port Campbell in Victoria.
facts.quote: a species of parrot endemic to eastern Australia ranging from Cooktown in Queensland to Port Campbell in Victoria.

facts.text: It prefers humid, heavily forested upland areas, including eucalyptus woodland beside subtropical and temperate rainforest.
facts.quote: Found in humid and heavily forested upland regions of the eastern portion of the continent, including eucalyptus wooded areas in and directly adjacent to subtropical and temperate rainforest.

facts.text: It feeds on fruits and seeds, gathering food from trees or on the ground.
facts.quote: They feed on fruits and seeds gathered from trees or on the ground.

facts.text: The male stands out with a red head and breast, a blue band on the back of the neck, green wings with pale green shoulder bands, and a blue rump.
facts.quote: The adult male has a red head, breast, and lower undersides, with a blue band on the back of the neck between the red above and green on the back, the wings are green and each has a pale green shoulder band, the tail is green, and the rump is blue.

facts.text: Females look very different from males, with a green head and breast, a grey beak, and a small or missing pale shoulder band.
facts.quote: The plumage of the female is very different from the male having a green head and breast, a grey beak, and the pale shoulder band is small or absent.

facts.text: Rare individuals lacking melanin have orange to yellow feathers and can look strikingly different from the usual scarlet and green birds.
facts.quote: On those rare individuals which have areas without melanin, feathers are orange to yellow. Such a bird can look startingly different from the more common scarlet and green variety.

facts.text: Canberra birders can spot king parrots in winter, when they venture beyond their normal eastern upland habitat.
facts.quote: Further from their normal eastern upland habitat, they are also found in Canberra during winter, the outer western and northern suburbs of Sydney, and the Carnarvon Gorge in central Queensland.

facts.text: Hand-raised king parrots make calm, relatively quiet household pets and can become very devoted to people.
facts.quote:
king parrots are occasionally bred in aviaries and kept as calm and relatively quiet household pets if hand-raised.
As pets, they have limited "talking" ability and normally prefer not to be handled, but they do bond readily to people and can be very devoted.

facts.text: Some pet king parrots have lived up to 25 years, though their lifespan in the wild is unknown.
facts.quote: Life expectancy in the wild is unknown, but some pets have been known to live up to 25 years.

facts.text: At a seed source, king parrots rank near the bottom of the pecking order, below galahs and just above crimson rosellas.
facts.quote: King parrots are near the bottom of the pecking order. At a food source of seeds, the approximate order is as follows: cockatoo, rainbow lorikeet, magpie, corella, galah, king parrot, crimson rosella.
